statement: A print shop offers three monthly plans. Plan A costs $20$ dollars plus $0.05$ dollar per page printed. Plan B costs $8$ dollars plus $0.11$ dollar per page. Plan C costs a flat $35$ dollars for any number of pages. For how many whole numbers of pages $n$, with $0 \le n \le 400$, is Plan A strictly cheaper than both of the other plans?

choices.misconception: I counted $n = 201$ through $n = 300$, but at 300 pages Plan A and Plan C both cost 35 dollars, so 300 does not count.
I compared Plan A only with Plan B, so I counted every value from 201 to 400 and forgot that Plan C is cheaper after 300 pages.
I counted every whole number from 200 through 300, including both tie points, where Plan A is not strictly cheaper.

hints: Plan A must beat Plan B and Plan C at the same time.
Solve $20 + 0.05n < 8 + 0.11n$ and $20 + 0.05n < 35$ separately, then count the whole numbers that satisfy both.
The first inequality gives $n > 200$ and the second gives $n < 300$. Count the whole numbers strictly between them.

solutions.reliable: Plan A beats Plan B when $20 + 0.05n < 8 + 0.11n$, so $12 < 0.06n$ and $n > 200$. Plan A beats Plan C when $20 + 0.05n < 35$, so $0.05n < 15$ and $n < 300$. The whole numbers with $200 < n < 300$ are $201, 202, \ldots, 299$, which is $299 - 201 + 1 = 99$ values. Key idea: 'cheaper than both' is a system of inequalities, so the answer is the overlap of two solution sets.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
